newsitem.title: USA: American Exploration works to cap blowout.
newsitem.headline: American Exploration works to cap blowout.

text.p: American Exploration Co said a drilling rig was moved in place over the weekend as crews worked to control and cap a natural gas well blowout on a production platform off the coast of Louisiana, company executives said on Monday.

The fire briefly reignited over the weekend, but the flow of natural gas shooting from the well has diminished and the plume now includes sizeable volumes of salt water and sand shooting about 30 feet into the sky, company executives said.

Crews will begin drilling the relief well by mid-week, and expect to intercept and divert the gas flows within two or three weeks to shut in the blowout and eventually cap the well, Elliott Pew, exploration vice president for the Houston-based company said.
"There is a chance the well may die out on its own before that, but we think it is prudent to continue on with our plans to drill the relief well," he said.
The blowout initially left a sheen of oil on the Gulf of Mexico, but the sheen quickly diminished and there have been no reports of other pollution, he said.

The well blew out last Tuesday after crews cemented it in and began removing safety equipment designed to prevent blowouts. Debris on the platform and the column of gas, water and sands shooting from the well have kept crews from capping the well.
The company could not measure the flow of gas from the well, Pew said.
